51949-horse-stories-and-stories-of-other.title: Horse Stories And Stories Of Other Animals
51949-horse-stories-and-stories-of-other.creator: Thomas W. Knox
51949-horse-stories-and-stories-of-other.description: A book by Thomas W. Knox. Their adventures in rearing and training two dogs, a Newfoundland and a Black-and-tan Terrier, are familiar to many young people. We are about to learn of their experience with horses and other quadrupeds, and will join them in listening to stories of animal intelligence in various parts of the world.

arabian-nights-burton-1885-vol-08.title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and a Night, Vol. 8
arabian-nights-burton-1885-vol-08.creator: Richard F. Burton (trans.)
arabian-nights-burton-1885-vol-08.description: Vol. 8 of Sir Richard Burton's unexpurgated 1885 literal translation of the Alf Layla wa Layla — the most famous and most cited English rendering of the Arabian Nights, with Burton's terminal essay and notes. Public domain. Sourced from Project Gutenberg ebook #3442 (https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/3442).

arxiv-1701-06239.title: Mining Shopping Patterns for Divergent Urban Regions by Incorporating Mobility Data Conference: CIKM’16 , October 24-28, 2016, Indianapolis, IN, USA Thanks: This work was conducted while the first author was doing internship at Microsoft Research Asia
arxiv-1701-06239.creator: Tianran Hu ∗1, Ruihua Song †2, Yingzi Wang †x3, Xing Xie †4, Jiebo Luo ∗5
arxiv-1701-06239.description: Abstract What people buy is an important aspect or view of lifestyles. Studying people’s shopping patterns in different urban regions can not only provide valuable information for various commercial opportunities, but also enable a better understanding about urban infrastructure and urban lifestyle. In this paper, we aim to predict city-wide shopping patterns.

arxiv-2101-03806.title: Multi-Domain Image-to-Image Translation with Adaptive Inference Graph
arxiv-2101-03806.creator: The-Phuc Nguyen, Stéphane Lathuilière, Elisa Ricci
arxiv-2101-03806.description: Abstract In this work, we address the problem of multi-domain image-to-image translation with particular attention paid to computational cost. In particular, current state of the art models require a large and deep model in order to handle the visual diversity of multiple domains. In a context of limited computational resources, increasing the network size may not be possible.

arxiv-2202-12615.title: Exact Solutions to Fall of Particle to Singular Potential: Classical vs. Quantum Cases
arxiv-2202-12615.creator: Michael I. Tribelsky
arxiv-2202-12615.description: Abstract Exact solutions describing a fall of a particle to the center of a non-regularized singular potential in classical and quantum cases are obtained and compared. We inspect the quantum problem with the help of the conventional Schrödinger’s equation. During the fall, the wave function spatial localization area contracts into a single zero-dimensional point.

arxiv-2302-00639.title: Extending the Q-score to an Application-level Quantum Metric Framework
arxiv-2302-00639.creator: Ward van der Schoot, Robert Wezeman, Niels M. P. Neumann, Frank Phillipson, Rob Kooij, Ward van der Schoot 1 3 , Robert Wezeman 1 , Niels Neumann 1 , Frank Phillipson 1 2
arxiv-2302-00639.description: Abstract Evaluating the performance of quantum devices is an important step towards scaling quantum devices and eventually using them in practice. The great number of available quantum metrics and the different hardware technologies used to develop quantum computers complicate this evaluation. In addition, different computational paradigms implement quantum operations in different ways.

arxiv-2305-07066.title: Mini-Quenching of z = 4 − 8 z=4-8 Galaxies by Bursty Star Formation 2023 Mini-Quenching of z = 4 − 8 z=4-8 Galaxies by Bursty Star Formation – References
arxiv-2305-07066.creator: Tibor Dome, Sandro Tacchella, Anastasia Fialkov, Daniel Ceverino, Avishai Dekel, Omri Ginzburg, Sharon Lapiner, Tobias J. Looser
arxiv-2305-07066.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tibor Dome, Sandro Tacchella, Anastasia Fialkov, Daniel Ceverino, Avishai Dekel, Omri Ginzburg, Sharon Lapiner, Tobias J. Looser. The recent reported discovery of a low-mass z = 5.2 z=5.2 and an intermediate-mass z = 7.3 z=7.3 quenched galaxy with JWST/NIRSpec is the first evidence of halted star formation above z ≈ 5 z\approx 5 .

arxiv-2308-15114.title: 2 2 -Coupon Coloring of Cubic Graphs Containing 3 3 -Cycle or 4 4 -Cycle
arxiv-2308-15114.creator: S. Akbari, M. Azimian, A. Fazli Khani, B. Samimi, E. Zahiri
arxiv-2308-15114.description: Abstract Let G G be a graph. A total dominating set in a graph G G is a set S S of vertices of G G such that every vertex in G G is adjacent to a vertex in S S .

arxiv-2408-05853.title: Predictors and Socio-Demographic Disparities in STEM Degree Outcomes: A UK Longitudinal Study using Hierarchical Logistic Regression
arxiv-2408-05853.creator: Andrew Low and Yasemin Kalender
arxiv-2408-05853.description: Abstract Socio-demographic disparities in STEM degree outcomes impact the diversity of the UK’s future workforce, particularly in fields essential for innovation and growth. Despite the importance of institution-level, longitudinal analyses in understanding degree awarding gaps, detailed multivariate and hierarchical analyses remain limited within the UK context.

arxiv-2412-20202.title: Revealing the Shape of Genome Space via K K -mer Topology
arxiv-2412-20202.creator: Yuta Hozumi and Guo-Wei Wei
arxiv-2412-20202.description: Abstract Despite decades of effort, understanding the shape of genome space in biology remains a challenge due to the similarity, variability, diversity, and plasticity of evolutionary relationships among species, genes, or other biological entities. We present a k k -mer topology method, the first of its kind, to delineate the shape of the genome space.

arxiv-2601-21654.title: ScholarGym: Benchmarking Deep Research Workflows on Academic Literature Retrieval
arxiv-2601-21654.creator: Hao Shen, Hang Yang, Zhouhong Gu
arxiv-2601-21654.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Hao Shen, Hang Yang, Zhouhong Gu. Tool-augmented large language models have advanced from single-turn question answering to deep research workflows that iteratively plan queries, invoke external tools, and synthesize information to address complex information needs. Evaluating such workflows presents a fundamental challenge: reliance on live APIs introduces non-determinism, as tool invocations may yield different results across runs due to temporal drift, rate limiting, and evolving backend states. This variance undermines reproducibility and invalidates cross-system comparisons.

pmc-11300814.title: A rare case of pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) presenting as short stature in an 8‐year‐old female
pmc-11300814.creator: Kamana Sen, Kritick Bhandari, Suman Simkhada, Karuna Humagain, Prasnna Basnet, Pawan Kumar Shah
pmc-11300814.description: Key Clinical MessagePituitary stalk interruption syndrome is a rare, congenital abnormality. Early identification and treatment can improve patient prognosis and quality of life and prevent adverse effect on growth and development. The patient described is an 8‐year‐old child with a history of short stature.

pmc-11460080.title: Unequal smiles: consequences of untreated dental caries in citizens living in vulnerable circumstances in the Netherlands: an exploratory pilot study
pmc-11460080.creator: Sterre J. Gitz, Geert J. M. G. van der Heijden, Catherine M.C. Volgenant
pmc-11460080.description: The often poor oral health status of socioeconomically vulnerable adults is widely recognised. Nevertheless, research on it is scarce. To address this gap, this exploratory pilot study aimed to report on the prevalence of untreated caries and its clinical odontogenic consequences, as well as the associated Oral Health Related Quality of Life (OHRQoL) in a marginalised adult Dutch population.

pmc-11672676.title: Impact of Removing the Monitoring Requirements for Holdings with Atypical Scrapie in Great Britain
pmc-11672676.creator: Mark Arnold, Bryony Jones, Verity Horigan, Robin Simons, Brenda Rajanayagam
pmc-11672676.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryAtypical scrapie (AS) is a disease of sheep and goats. Currently, when AS is detected on a farm in Great Britain (GB), all animals that exit the flock through natural death or slaughter are tested for AS for a period of 2 years following detection of the initial case, as used to be performed within the European Union (EU), in order to provide support as to whether AS can transmit directly between sheep.

pmc-11675750.title: The Impact of Disease X on Potential Travelers’ Travel Decision
pmc-11675750.creator: Robertico Croes, Jeong-Yeol Park, Kenneth Alexander, Chaithanya Renduchintala, Frank Badu-Baiden
pmc-11675750.description: This study used ANCOVA models to investigate how pandemic characteristics—spreading speed, severity, and vaccination requirements—affect travel intentions. The results reveal that these factors explain 31.7% of the variance in travel decisions, with disease-spreading speed and severity being the most significant determinants. While vaccination requirements are relevant, they play a secondary role compared to the immediate threat of disease characteristics.

pmc-11715728.title: Preliminary analysis reveals links between visual attention, sleep duration, and neural recruitment in Alzheimer's disease
pmc-11715728.creator: Maggie P Rempe, Seth D Springer, Grant M Garrison, Ryan J Glesinger, Hannah J Okelberry, Aubrie J Petts, Christine M Embury, Tony W Wilson
pmc-11715728.description: BackgroundSleep disturbances have been shown to relate to the development of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and its associated cognitive deficits, including visual attention function. Here, we investigated the potential interactive and additive effects of sleep disruption and AD on visual attention performance and its underlying neural mechanisms.

pmc-11716220.title: Psychosis in Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11716220.creator: Clive G Ballard
pmc-11716220.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Psychosis is a common and distressing disorder in people with Alzheimer disease, associated with a poor clinical prognosis, an increased risk of institutionalization and for which there are no approved treatments. New approaches to diagnosis and symptom assessment and treatment are beginning to move the field forward, including the emergence of psychosis at the pre‐clinical or even pre‐cognitive impairment stages of disease in some individuals.

pmc-12369067.title: Predictors of trachoma among children aged 1–9 years in Ethiopia: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12369067.creator: Shambel Dessale Asmamaw, Birhan Alemnew
pmc-12369067.description: IntroductionTrachoma is one of the leading chronic diseases in children 1–9 years old and a cause of death primary in resources limited countries. Even though unlimited efforts have been undertaken to control the disease, it remains a major public health challenge in developing nations.

pmc-12502901.title: High‐Resolution 3‐Dimensional Micro‐CT Imaging of Intervertebral Discs Using a Novel Contrast Agent
pmc-12502901.creator: Madison M Buckles, Abdulkadir Nur, Nada H Warda, Jacob C Moncher, Mohammad Yunus Ansari
pmc-12502901.description: BackgroundThe nucleus pulposus (NP) in the intervertebral disc (IVD) is the first structure to exhibit degenerative changes during IVD degeneration (IDD). Currently, micro‐computed tomography (micro‐CT) imaging of the NP is a limiting factor in detecting IDD at an early stage. While contrast‐enhanced micro‐CT has been investigated, an effective contrast agent for IVD has not been identified.

pmc-12940240.title: Restoration of Defective CFTR in Human Nasal Respiratory Epithelial Cells by CFTR Modulators and mRNA Transfection
pmc-12940240.creator: Roshani Narayan Singh, Marilia Marta Horn, Marin Juko, Ami Kampshoff, Jochen Schmid, Heymut Omran, Dandan Zhang, Joseph Rosenecker, Wolf-Michael Weber, Jörg Große-Onnebrink
pmc-12940240.description: The cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) is a member of the atypical ATP-binding cassette (ABC) family that functions as a phosphorylation-regulated epithelial anion channel. Cystic fibrosis (CF) is characterised by variants in the CFTR gene that lead to impaired epithelial chloride–ion transport and increased mucus viscosity.

pmc-13463793.title: Not as information, but as a trigger: recurrent climate trauma after the 2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods
pmc-13463793.creator: Samuel Paulo Cibulski
pmc-13463793.description: ressure. Many neighbours already exhibit signs of anxiety and depression that arose after the loss of everything they had: homes, crops, animals, memories. In May 2024, the worst climate disaster in southern Brazil affected nearly 2·4 million people, displacing more than 580,000.
